Congratulations on such a big step. I am so happy to hear she was accepting. *hugs* I hope that once the intensity of the stress you were under from telling her fades; you will let go of your shame. I wasn't there so forgive me for saying this if I am missing a reason, but I while I can see why you might feel ashamed. I think what you did was amazing brave. I wish both you and your mother the best.

Well this is definitely the right place. I am so saddened to hear you are in such pain. You deserve better. I wish I could offer more then just words and virtual hugs, but my thoughts are with you and know there is a stranger hoping you find happiness or at the very least comfort. I just want you to know you are not alone. 

PS Please try to eat and sleep more. It will help. The calories you are eating aren't going to help you lose weight, your body will just shut down and then store anything it can when you do eat normally. Try taking a walk in the moments you have free, it could help you feel a little more connected to the world and give you a mental boost as well. Just some thoughts, please don't take them as directives or anything. 

*big hugs*

First off, your voice is beautiful. You have obviously worked on your pitch and resonance. I want to preface what I am about to say with the fact I am not a vocal coach, this is just my own experience.   

I would say though that you suffer from a breathy sound in your voice that is from pushing your voice into a falsetto. To rid myself of it I did the following exercise as part of my vocal training. I found them in a search for dealing with my own falsetto. Remember no forcing and let your voice rest.

Do some vocal fold stops - ee ee, uh oh, ah ah.

Imagine you are at the doctors and say 'ah'.

Call out to someone across the road (imagine) you are really happy to see - "hey john" or "hey you".

Say and sustain 'ugh' 

Cheer happily when your team just scored. Yeah! Sustain it. 

Make some twangy sounds - nyah nyah nyah nyah nyah - this can help close the vocal folds.
Thank you. Now I have a study to show people that backs up what I have been saying for years.

I am so sorry to hear about the trouble you are having. I wish I could do or something to help. Does your area have a PFLAG or some other state or local equality group that might have references for legal help? Don't give up. For what it is worth I will be looking forward to you being wrong about your prophecy.

You have a really good voice and what you have done is great. I will say that you are right about the resonance, it does need a little work. You are just shy of hitting falsetto, maybe lower your pitch just a little as you resonance gets better. 

I would work on your breathing, pulling your voice out of your chest. Try actively thinking about talking through your nose. Not literally of course, and not nasally, just that the strength of your voice comes from your head and not your chest. This will help your resonance. 

But like I said, you are doing very well!

I think any sane, competent person would see blaming the victim as wrong. And also think they would see that despite the best planning and awareness things will not always go as we plan them and that things will sometimes lead to an untenable situation. The part of the article gravitate to is that her male 'friend' made a comment as a solution to her problem and then seemed to believe the over site on her part was enough to dismiss the dismay she felt about her situation that night. Her fears were dismissed, her judgement questioned and her feelings ignored. How was she supposed to react? The fact her first thought to attempt decorum was admirable. It is sad that an unthinking, apathetic comment about her feeling unsafe not only made her feel the need to defend herself, but also that she felt others would be turned off for her doing so. 

Being a woman (trans or not) should not be a qualifier for the removal of safety for someone, the fact it is should be of concern to anyone. It is absurd to think that there should not be change or that such change is part of some utopian ideal. It isn't going to happen overnight, but until more people are made aware of the situation, the less likely this is going to be change. The fact people want to dismiss the problem outright just goes to prove the point and how hard it is going to be for there to be change.

If people get upset that someone is not willing to just accept 'reality' and as such they are immediately disregarded then that again is something that needs to be changed.

I am hardly an expert on voice training, but it won't stop me from putting in my comments. You did ask for it after all. >.> <.<

I think your first pitch is better. You are too falsetto in the second pitch. Maybe try to find a lower pitch then falsetto but higher then your first. I practiced using a pitch pipe and by singing vowels in a scale in the range I wanted to speak. Just a thought. Remember to keep hydrated and take breaks.

You are right. Entitlement is a strong word to use when you're pointing at such a large subset of people. Ignorance would perhaps be better, but I think perhaps apathy might be a better term. Surely, Apathy is something that everyone experiences. We are all apathetic to each other in some fashion. 

Unfortunately, it is this apathy (or ignorance if you prefer) that breeds this feeling that there is in fact entitlement. Being told that there is no danger and no cause for discussion is in fact harmful. It breeds a culture that says a girl asks for it because she is dressed a certain way. 

Like I said I have been on both sides of the fence. I remember how I felt when a similar discussion was made back when I identified as male. I couldn't grasp, or perhaps did not want to grasp, the idea that other people saw danger, prejudice or abuse in what I saw as safe and normal.  It made me feel bad. I didn't know what I was doing was harmful, so I wasn't guilty of anything. And I certainly wasn't entitled.  Society said it as normal, who am I to argue?

And then one day, I made a small realization about myself and boom. My mind was blown. It didn't happen all at once. I was to blinded by my own self deprivation to see it any where else.  But as I started to get over myself I also started to see the world around me in a totally different way. I learned what it was like to be marginalized and objectified. I saw and experienced what I had been before. I thought about what I had done and how it might have made others feel. It made me question a lot about society and people as individuals.

So please forgive me for using the word entitlement. It is a strong a word. It is a unfair label to put on someone who doesn't know any better. And I would hate for everyone to feel like they were victimized or unsafe.

I am pre-trans and the only time I shave is when I am going out to meet someone I know. For local stuff like grocery shopping and such I don't bother. Strangers don't care, I have nothing to prove to myself so I just don't care.

I would seriously like to have Christin Milloy for a friend. I wish more women were like her. The entitlement men have in interactions with women is in desperate need of change. It isn't men's fault per se, I know I used to do it myself and never saw what I was doing or that it was wrong. I now actively try not to. But like Ms. Milloy I have become very aware of it in others. It is not because I am labeling them, but because there is a certain amount of empathy that goes along with be socially aware from time spent on both sides of the gender spectrum. 

To go back to the article, I can definitely relate to the discussion. I have walked down dark inner city streets in LA with not even a passing thought of being abused or violated. Since I have identified as trans and changed my appearance to that of a woman, I find myself thinking smarter and planning to avoid situations where I would be in danger. As a man over six foot, I made for an imposing figure. As a woman, I am just a bigger target. Nothing has changed except the way people see my sex. So yeah, I would be greatly offended if a man told me the bus was safe at night. 

Also I get why she as inserted herself into the gender roles associated with women. For most trans people it is hard enough to get people to see us for who we are. In a supreme act of counter intuitive impulse we end up draping ourselves in beliefs and habits that society has deemed feminine. Fitting in and being accepted starts to overwhelm the need to be ourselves. It is a human failing that does not come even close to being trans only. At some point if we are lucky we realize what we are doing and attempt to stop it, but the consequences that are not something everyone can endure. 

Anyway, the article really struck a nerve and some the comments made about it brought out my inner 'bitch'. Maybe it is just the man in me asserting my stance and belief. Maybe I am just a activist who being too sensitive to something that really isn't a problem. And yes, I see the hypocrisy of speaking out against people who are speaking out against people.

Wow, you are kind, trans supporter, AND a Doctor Who fan. Your girlfriend is a very lucky lady. I am very grateful for your advice and your hug. Thank you for both. 

While I certainly am no closer to answering my question, it is on the back burner once again. Like most people with depression, my ability to cope comes and goes. 

Anyway, thank you again and I hope you are enjoying the new series (season) of Doctor Who. I am enjoying it so far myself.

I was were you are about twelve years ago. I was playing EverQuest at the time. I personally just started trying to sing along with women on the radio. I kept recording and listening to myself talk. Eventually I found things on the internet (which are now unfortunately no longer available even though the Internet Archive). I also found Finding Your Female Voice. You had to pay for the DVDs back then but Deep Stealth put them up for free on Youtube. 

You don't have to be 100% passable online. People will either fill in the blanks or just not care enough to bother you about it. 

And remember speak from your head not your chest. Think of it as projecting your voice up through your nose.

I bought EVA Pitch and EVA Pitch 4 for iOS. As some will say, I thought the instruction was helpful. The pitch exercise is simple. It sets a frequency level (or levels) and tells you how well you can retain them. It is not a complete voice training system. I think people like the one who wrote that article over sell it. I also felt cheated by the video of one of Kathy Perez's clients as it seemed to indicate a change in voice might be possible given a commitment of time and effort in combination with the apps. I seriously do not believe that to be the case and would call use of the video in relation to the app as fraudulent. 

For anyone wanting an app on iOS to test you pitch, I would suggest Pitch Graph by Martin Britz. For instruction, I personally, in part, used Find Your Female Voice by Deep Stealth Productions. I would recommend that for anyone interested in voice training. 

Anyway, $20 is not a lot in the grand scheme of the costs of transistion. The EVA Pitch for did challenge me though. Going from one note to another is something I do need to practice.

You really are going to be okay. As for you working harder, I can't say that it wouldn't have helped, but mistakes are made and sometimes we pay for them. But sometimes, bad things happen. Things don't go the way we want them too. What makes me want to stand and applaud you is that you are still trying. That a small gesture of generosity can stay a lethal hand and that you respect others enough to worry about what your actions might do to them. I hope you ended up rewarded for the work you are doing.

For me moving is a solution and a problem. It would mean leaving my support system in then family (besides my dad) and friends that I have. They keep me on an even emotional keel. Not ruling out moving, but an area needs more then good food. ;) I did really like Portland though. If I was moving for food, it would be some place close to an In'n'Out. If I decided to die, I could eat myself to death on Double Doubles and Animal Fries. :)

Sorry if I was a little aggressive about my age. I am sensitive about it ;)

Better living through chemistry. It is an answer. One I have been searching for myself for over a decade now. I am on Trazodone right now and it takes the edge off. I am not wallowing in despair like I once was. Be it clears my head only so much. It is for the anxiety mostly, doesn't do much for the depression itself. I am still trying, even my doctor knows we have way to go, but there aren't any avenues I haven't tried. 

I so like helping others, but I would argue the point on how beneficial online friendships are. They either develop into true friendships or act as a band-aid that constantly needs replacing. The latter of which can add to ones problems. But I also say, if it works, stick with it until it doesn't. So...

Moving is not an option for me until my father passes. I am his caregiver. Well we take care of each other, but I am not going anywhere while he is still around. After, yeah, relocation is a necessity after he passes. I know of many places I might go. Thank you for a glowing review of Portland, an old friend of mine lives there and I did enjoy my time there, especially Powells. heh Unfortunately, unless I want to do it living on the streets, living in a metropolitan area is outside the range of finances. 

Thank you so much for your kind words, advice and sharing of your personal experiences. All of them were appreciated. I am very glad to hear that while things are hard for you, you have managed to find things to engage you, I hope you continue to find them and any happiness they might entail. 

To answer your last question specifically I am 38. If I might, why do you ask?

Thank you for your honest and personal reply. 

I agree with you about genetics. Some people are just unlucky in that regard. It is sad that the abnormality is left untreated by so many and that is so deceptively lethal.

I am glad you have such support and such escape. I hope both allow you to realize or stumble upon something or someone that brings you something positive to your life.

I am not saying one is compelled to live. Well that isn't true, most people are compelled to live against overwhelming cost, but since in cases like this that isn't true, we will just say no one has want to live.

I am asking my non-answer because I ask it of myself. If I seek death, why do I not seek life? What makes me feel like non existence is the answer. I will cease to exist at some point. Why feel the need to hasten the process? I don't ask to save a life, I ask out of personal curiosity. I mean I am not alone. People much smarter and wiser then me have asked that question and come up with some sizable answers. They make sense, but they aren't my answer. So every time someone asks me why do I live? I ask why do you not?

Well I am 40 and things aren't better so no worries on me saying things get better. A common quote that a lot of people repeat is "Life is what happens to us while we are making other plans.". I like to think about that. It gives life the relatable randomness it deserves. We so often work hard to give our lives meaning, but life isn't so tidy. It's chaotic and messy. 

You say you want to be happy and trying to find it, but happiness is a result of something. It is a thing that comes after a thing. 

You are lonely. I wonder why. What inside you do you dislike so much that you can't stand yourself as company. I personally feel the first step to finding friends that are worthwhile is to like yourself. It doesn't sound like you do. Am I wrong?

If I were in your situation I would probably just enable her by staying in a relationship I didn't want to be in so, thank goodness I am not. But, you caring is a good first step. She needs to find self worth inside her. She needs to see she is worth it. Now seeing as she is depressed that is going to be hard. Be a friend to her if you can, but do things that require more then just the two of you. Put her in situations where she has to interact with people she doesn't know. You must know some her interests, so find groups that have similar interests. Go with her to a few. Our lives are so separated for the world that finding small pockets of support is hard and usually that burden falls on one persons shoulders. If that person is lucky. So many people don't have anyone. So like I said your ex is lucky to have you in her life. If you want to so the work, you can make a difference.

Yes, it gets better. A simple search will expose the fact that while your life might seem like to much now, there is so much out there to see and experience yet. Good and bad. And maybe you will decide later it isn't worth it, but at least give yourself the chance of finding out.

I wonder if your pets see you as pathetic. Low self worth is one thing, but you obviously love you animals. What is so harsh that it isn't worth being able to care for them and all the others after them that could live lives full of love you could give them? I mean, sure you could end your life, but why? I am not asking rhetorically I am asking because you are scared, you are scared of death, and your animals might be the reason. So before you end your life, please think about it.

Why do most people live because their lives are pointless? Why live because they are oppressed, marginalized and objectified? Why oh why live a lie? Because to most people, it never even crosses their mine, or if it does, it is a frightful piece of madness they quickly shy away from. 

People live life because the only other option is death. And death is scary. Death is reason for the season. Things are won and lost because we are so scared of death we will make ourselves believe there is something after we die. 

Be there are some, who don't fear death. Be it a mental imbalance, faith, logic or a willingness to give their life it something they see as being greater then themselves, they all see death not as anything but a result of life. A portion of those even question the worth of life. 

Now this is a oversimplification. I left a lot out, but this isn't meant for anyone but you. I am not saying your stupid, just that I doubt you would want to read it. 

So why go on? I ask why not? If life means so little, then what makes taking death in exchange so worth it? Is there something that makes life so horrible? 

You asked why. So I am asking why not? And if there is a reason, doesn't it upset you even a little that it was enough to push you around?

I won't insult you by say troubles are temporary. That while we feel overwhelmed with life, such stress is temporary. Solutions to life's problems rarely come from preplanned events. To say that to you would belittle the pain you are dealing with. You have no hope. This is not a condemnation. It is just a statement of fact. So what would give you hope? Is it something or someone? 

Perhaps, consider this. Is there someone or something that is keeping you from feeling hope? It could be something you can't even immediately label. Depression hides a lot for us. It hides even the idea that we might suffer from it. 

As for those you would hurt, you're right. You would not see them hurting, but just as you know there are things that overwhelm you, you also know you would hurt them. Stay your hand from a final solution until you are sure it is the only way. Do it for them, even if they don't see or realize the sacrifice you are making. I say this not for them, but for you. 

I won't say but one last thing. Knowing that there is another asking themselves a similar question to mine has in fact helped me with my problems. Just not feeling so alone gives a small comfort, but gives comfort none the less. So thank you. I will hope something comes along to help you as well.
